say: This is AIOS: my personal AI operating system.
It turns several AI models into one team that works on my projects, remembers what it has learned, and asks before it does anything important.
Most AI tools start every conversation from zero, in their own window, with their own rules.
I wanted one system where the models share context, follow the same rules, and stay under my control.
AIOS is built in layers.
At the top is a desktop control panel.
Under it runs ClaudeOS, powered by Claude Code, which owns the system. Codex joins as an expert partner for reviews and second opinions.
Routine work goes to fast workers: Groq in the cloud, and Ollama models running locally on my Mac.
Inside ClaudeOS, named agents have clear roles.
MoMo coordinates the work.
CoCo builds, and runs engineering loops.
FiFi does the research.
A Groq research agent searches the web, and local Ollama models handle private or bulk tasks at no cost.
Memory lives in the Second Brain: a shared folder of plain files that every agent reads before it starts.
Hot memory holds current tasks, messages and decisions.
Each project keeps its own memory and handoff notes, and older knowledge moves to cold storage.
It is all versioned in git, so every change can be traced.
Rules come first.
A shared contract and a list of prohibited actions apply to every agent.
Anything risky, like merging code, pushing to git or deleting files, becomes a proposal in the approval inbox, in English and Finnish, and waits for my decision.
A scheduler built on Node-RED runs tasks on its own.
Nightly maintenance, a memory organiser that keeps the Second Brain tidy, and research loops.
Every run writes a log, and failures show up as alerts.
The control panel is an Electron desktop app.
A live graph shows the Second Brain and how it connects.
Charts track usage for each provider,
and from one chat box I can talk to any agent, run a task, or approve an inbox item.
Away from the desk, AIOS Remote lets me ask for status or file a note by voice, from my iPhone.
One team of models. One shared memory. Clear rules.
That's AIOS.
